source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 1 (i)-(iv): cosine of the angle between two vectors (book p.274). Answers agree with the key (PDF 311).

blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the cosines of the angle \(\theta\) between \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\): \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = -\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do vectors components mein diye hain aur humein un ke beech ke angle ka cosine chahiye, angle khud nahi.
Diya kya hai? \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ke components.
Find kya karna hai? \(\cos\theta\).
Rule kaunsa? Dot product ki do shaklein: \(\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\) aur \(\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = a_1a_2 + b_1b_2 + c_1c_2\). Dono ko barabar rakh kar \(\cos\theta\) nikal aata hai.
Plan: pehle dot product, phir dono magnitudes, phir divide.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = -\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\cos\theta\), jahan \(\theta\) dono vectors ke beech ka angle hai.
Tareeqa: \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v}}{|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|}\). Yeh formula definition \(\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\) ko \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\) se divide kar ke milta hai. Components se dot product nikalna bohat aasaan hai (matching components multiply kar ke jama), aur lengths bhi components se mil jati hain. Is liye angle seedha naapne ki zaroorat nahi parti.

Dot product nikalein
\[\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = (2)(-1) + (3)(2) + (1)(2)\]
\[= -2 + 6 + 2 = 6\]
Kyun: Dot product mein \(\underline{i}\) ko \(\underline{i}\) se, \(\underline{j}\) ko \(\underline{j}\) se aur \(\underline{k}\) ko \(\underline{k}\) se multiply kar ke jama karte hain. Wajah yeh hai ke \(\underline{i}\cdot\underline{i} = \underline{j}\cdot\underline{j} = \underline{k}\cdot\underline{k} = 1\) hai, lekin \(\underline{i}\cdot\underline{j}\) jaise mixed products zero hain, kyunke yeh unit vectors aapas mein perpendicular hain. Is liye sirf matching components bachte hain.
Dhyan dein: minus sign wale component ka product likhte waqt bracket zaroor lagaiye, warna sign ghalat ho jata hai.

Dono magnitudes nikalein
\[|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{14}\]
\[|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 2^2 + 2^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{9} = 3\]
Kyun: Kisi vector \(a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}\) ki length (magnitude) \(\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}\) hoti hai; yeh space mein Pythagoras hi hai. Square karne se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye har term positive jama hoti hai.
Dhyan dein: \((-3)^2 = 9\) hai, \(-9\) nahi.

Formula mein rakh kar divide karein
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{14}\,(3)} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{14}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2\sqrt{14}}{14} = \dfrac{\sqrt{14}}{7}\]
Kyun: Teeno numbers formula mein rakhe. 6 aur 3 mein se 3 cancel hua to \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{14}}\) bacha. Answer key wali shakal mein lane ke liye upar neeche \(\sqrt{14}\) se multiply kiya (rationalise kiya, yani neeche se root hataya): \(\frac{2\sqrt{14}}{14} = \frac{\sqrt{14}}{7}\). Dono jawab barabar hain.

Tasdeeq
\[\cos\theta \approx 0.5345\]
\[\theta \approx 57.7^{\circ}\]
Kyun: \(\cos\theta\) hamesha \(-1\) aur 1 ke beech hota hai; humara jawab is range mein hai. Dot product positive tha, is liye angle acute (90 degree se chhota) hona chahiye tha, aur \(57.7^{\circ}\) acute hi hai. Jawab maqool hai.

\[\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = (5)(3) + (-2)(4) + (1)(2)\]
\[= 15 - 8 + 2 = 9\]

\[|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{25 + 4 + 1} = \sqrt{30}\]
\[|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{9 + 16 + 4} = \sqrt{29}\]

Tasdeeq
\[\sqrt{870} \approx 29.50\]
\[\cos\theta \approx 0.305,\ \theta \approx 72.2^{\circ}\]
Kyun: Value \(-1\) aur 1 ke beech hai aur positive hai, kyunke dot product 9 positive tha. Is liye angle acute hai. Sab kuch aapas mein milta hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find the cosines of the angle \(\theta\) between \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\): \(\underline{u} = [-3, 2, 5]\), \(\underline{v} = [1, 6, -2]\)

Yahan do vectors components mein diye hain aur humein un ke beech ke angle ka cosine chahiye, angle khud nahi.

Plan: pehle dot product, phir dono magnitudes, phir divide.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{u} = [-3, 2, 5] = -3\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = [1, 6, -2] = \underline{i} + 6\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\cos\theta\), jahan \(\theta\) dono vectors ke beech ka angle hai.
Tareeqa: \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v}}{|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|}\). Yeh formula definition \(\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\) ko \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\) se divide kar ke milta hai. Components se dot product nikalna bohat aasaan hai (matching components multiply kar ke jama), aur lengths bhi components se mil jati hain. Is liye angle seedha naapne ki zaroorat nahi parti.

Dot product nikalein
\[\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = (-3)(1) + (2)(6) + (5)(-2)\]
\[= -3 + 12 - 10 = -1\]
Kyun: Dot product mein \(\underline{i}\) ko \(\underline{i}\) se, \(\underline{j}\) ko \(\underline{j}\) se aur \(\underline{k}\) ko \(\underline{k}\) se multiply kar ke jama karte hain. Wajah yeh hai ke \(\underline{i}\cdot\underline{i} = \underline{j}\cdot\underline{j} = \underline{k}\cdot\underline{k} = 1\) hai, lekin \(\underline{i}\cdot\underline{j}\) jaise mixed products zero hain, kyunke yeh unit vectors aapas mein perpendicular hain. Is liye sirf matching components bachte hain.
Dhyan dein: minus sign wale component ka product likhte waqt bracket zaroor lagaiye, warna sign ghalat ho jata hai.

Dono magnitudes nikalein
\[|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{9 + 4 + 25} = \sqrt{38}\]
\[|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{1 + 36 + 4} = \sqrt{41}\]
Kyun: Kisi vector \(a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}\) ki length (magnitude) \(\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}\) hoti hai; yeh space mein Pythagoras hi hai. Square karne se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye har term positive jama hoti hai.
Dhyan dein: \((-3)^2 = 9\) hai, \(-9\) nahi.

Formula mein rakh kar divide karein
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{38}\,\sqrt{41}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{1558}}\]
Kyun: \(38 \times 41 = 1558\). Bracket wali shakal \([a, b, c]\) se ghabraiye nahi: yeh sirf \(a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}\) likhne ka chhota tareeqa hai, pehla number \(\underline{i}\) ka, doosra \(\underline{j}\) ka, teesra \(\underline{k}\) ka.

Tasdeeq
\[\cos\theta \approx -0.0253\]
\[\theta \approx 91.4^{\circ}\]
Kyun: Dot product negative aaye to angle obtuse (90 degree se bara) hota hai. Yahan \(-1\) lengths ke muqable mein bohat chhota hai, is liye angle 90 degree se bas zara sa bara hai. Vectors taqreeban perpendicular hain, lekin bilkul nahi.
Dhyan dein: Negative cosine ko ghalti mat samjhiye; yeh sirf obtuse angle ki nishani hai.

steps:

\[\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = (2)(2) + (-3)(4) + (1)(1)\]
\[= 4 - 12 + 1 = -7\]
Kyun: Dot product mein \(\underline{i}\) ko \(\underline{i}\) se, \(\underline{j}\) ko \(\underline{j}\) se aur \(\underline{k}\) ko \(\underline{k}\) se multiply kar ke jama karte hain.
